objective: Platform engineering goals, objectives and approaches: reducing cognitive load, paved roads, golden paths, platform as a product, and the CNCF Platforms white paper's capabilities

sources.cite: CNCF Certified Cloud Native Platform Engineering Associate (CNPA) curriculum: Platform Engineering Core Fundamentals 36%, Platform Observability, Security and Conformance 20%, Continuous Delivery and Platform Engineering 16%, Platform APIs and Provisioning Infrastructure 12%, IDPs and Developer Experience 8%, Measuring your Platform 8%
sources.note: On 2026-11-17 the weights were confirmed through a third-party study page (kube-dojo.github.io/k8s/cnpa, summarizing fetch), which lists 'GitOps fundamentals' and continuous delivery in the core fundamentals domain and says to 'understand why GitOps uses pull-based reconciliation'. The official curriculum was not re-read; the objective wording is the course seed's. Reused for REQ-336 from this course's service-selector-no-endpoints-cnpa (the same reading and date); the objective wording is the course seed's.

sources.cite: CNCF TAG App Delivery, CNCF Platforms White Paper
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 with WebFetch (a summarizing fetch) of the primary page, found by WebSearch. Confirms: platforms reduce the cognitive load on product teams; platforms are designed from their users' requirements, learned through interviews, surveys and usage observation, with product managers sharing roadmaps; a golden path is a bundled template with documentation; platforms should be optional and composable, self-service and thin; success is measured by user satisfaction (for example NPS) and active users and retention.
The organization, the systems and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You lead a new platform team at Brookvale Health Software, a fictional company with 22 product teams. Each team runs its own pipelines, clusters and dashboards; onboarding a service takes three weeks.
handover: The CTO wants 'one platform for everyone' by summer.
Two teams built their own internal tools and fear losing them.
howItWorks: The board shows the risk register against the appetite, each stakeholder's support in words and the docket.
Move on a week at a time. A decision comes to you at each review; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Week 2: teams fork their pipelines to keep working; the two in-house tool owners escalate to the CTO.
Week 3: the data team's model training stops; they cannot add GPU jobs to the locked template.
Week 4: adoption hits 95% on paper while half the teams keep shadow pipelines; satisfaction is never asked.

goalPrompt.title: What the platform is for
goalPrompt.context: The CTO asks for a one-line goal.

choices.label: Goal: reduce product teams' cognitive load so a new service ships in a day; the platform is a product with a product manager, built from the interviews and a public roadmap
choices.feedback: Platforms exist to serve their users and reduce their cognitive load; a product mindset starts from user research.

choices.label: Goal: standardize on the platform team's preferred tools
choices.feedback: Consistency helps, but it starts from the platform team's taste, not users' needs.

choices.label: Goal: one mandatory platform; retire every team's tools by summer
choices.feedback: Forcing adoption before the platform serves users breeds workarounds.

pathPrompt.title: What teams get first
pathPrompt.context: Pipelines, secrets and dashboards cost the most time.

choices.label: A golden path template: repository, pipeline, secrets wiring and dashboards with docs; optional and composable, so the data team can use parts and keep its GPU jobs

effects.log: Three teams adopt it in a week.

choices.feedback: A golden path bundles a well-integrated template with docs; optional and composable platforms win adoption.

choices.label: Publish a wiki page of recommended tools
A single locked template no team may change
choices.feedback: The data team cannot run GPU jobs; teams needing anything different are blocked.

measurePrompt.title: How do we know it works?
measurePrompt.context: The CTO wants a number by quarter end.

choices.label: Track satisfaction (a short quarterly survey with NPS), active teams and retention, and time to first deploy, and review them with teams

effects.log: Measures and a review cadence are agreed.

choices.feedback: A platform is measured like a product: user satisfaction and active users and retention.

choices.label: Count templates created
choices.feedback: Counts what the platform made, not whether it helped.

choices.label: Make 100% adoption by quarter end every team's KPI
choices.feedback: Teams adopt on paper and keep side tools; the number means nothing.

reflection.question: Write the platform charter for the CTO and the product teams.

parts.label: Goal and offering
parts.criteria: Reduce cognitive load; optional, composable golden path.
parts.modelAnswer: The platform is a product that lets a team ship a new service in a day; the first golden path covers repo, pipeline, secrets and dashboards, and teams can use parts.

parts.label: Measures
parts.criteria: Satisfaction, active teams and retention, time to first deploy.
parts.modelAnswer: We survey teams quarterly, track active teams and time to first deploy, and review them together.

scoring.modelReasoning: Platform engineering exists to reduce product teams' cognitive load. Run the platform as a product: learn users' needs, offer optional, composable golden paths with docs, and measure user satisfaction and active use rather than mandating adoption.
